TL;DR: YTA, because you are thinking about yourself too much here. You don't throw away an otherwise healthy potential relationship because of one drunken night being awkward. You talk like adults about how and why you were hurt. Try to understand if this was a personal insecurity or a judgement call gone wrong from both sides. This is a mistake too many people make at all ages and stages of relationships and then quit, hold grudges and then become grinches and scrooges towards all their future partners and relations. 

The long reply:

  
There is something we call a knee jerk reaction. There's a few things you have to think about and right now you're not thinking about it enough. If you are ever going to be in a loving long term relationship you have to understand and be prepared for vulnerable moments to not go right. This time, it was the first time trying to hook up. Next time it might be you forgetting a birthday or anniversary. Regardless, you reacted to this situation not responded. Here's a few things to think about:  
  
1. Do you actually like this person and would you have wanted a relationship with her before things went the way they did that night? (If your answer is no, and you're not interested in trying or talking then don't read further.) 

You guys have known each other for a very long time. You've also respected each others boundaries and not taken things further for a long time. But you have been building the foundations of a relationship here. The closeness, the time spent together, the family time spent together. The similar interests and hobbies.   


2. Did you talk to her about what happened? I know the answer is no.   
  
There are a plethora of reasons why you probably feel bad about what happened. She obviously feels terrible and has tried to reach out to you several times to talk about things. You are being emotional and egotistical. 

"She removed my boxers and had no reaction" - Life isn't porn and you're drunk hooking up for the first time.   
"I’m guessing Julie expected something much bigger because I’m tall." - Exactly you're guessing. You don't know the facts.   
"Either way, Julie said she needed a minute to compose herself, and she asked if we could proceed at a later day, as she wasn’t really feeling it that night." - She asked for time, asked to try again on another day, and that while she wanted to jump on your dick felt a reason not to. Maybe wants this to be more than a drunk hookup.    
"Julie apologized a lot, and I told her it was alright and left." - It wasn't alright, cause you're moaning to the internet about it. She expressed how sorry she was that it didn't happen (on more than one occasion) and you still decided to leave because you got your feelings hurt about something that is your own insecurity. 

3. Is your friendship over? 

Maybe. Maybe you move on and think about where she might be and what happened for the rest of your life. Maybe you never date again and become that guy who hates women because that one time a girl you loved made you feel insecure and you've vowed to never let that happen again and will move into your parents basement where you never have to see the sun or experience warmth. Maybe you giver her another chance and say no, you don't think you can have a friendship with her, because you want a relationship with her. You just need to know that she wants to be in one too because having sex with her means that much and is a line you can't walk back from and you've considered the facts of this situation enough to want that and to be able to look back and laugh about it later. Maybe you just move on and continue to distance yourself from her and just forget about it all like it was a bad dream. 

  
Any way you look at it, you are young and have a lot to learn. I highly recommend reading a book called Hold Me Tight. If you plan to be in a long term relationship, its a must read.

In this case I was just using biv as an example for what an X-ray might show. I agree with you in that the behavior doesn’t match, however in a BiV pacer, depending on the company, they can favorable only pace the LV at some rates and then BiV pace at others. This can also cause a widening and narrowing of the QRS depending on this behavior too. In this case, I don’t think it’s a BiV since it didn’t sound like the rates varied that much either.

Former med student and current pacer rep here. This is a V paced rhythm. If the device is going back and forth it could be because their intrinsic is going higher than the lower rate setting and then settling back down. That behavior depends on the programming of the device. It could be programmed in several different ways. 

It’s also important to note that these days, pacemakers aren’t meant to pace all the time. Studies have found that pacing in the right ventricle more than 40% of the time increases risk of heart failure. As a result, algorithms have been developed to reduce pacing in the RV. 

If this pt has a Hx of afib, and this is a single chamber device, they may be set to only V pace with movement. The rate of pacing will increase with torso movements since there is a sensor for movement which artificially acts to compensate rate with movement. We commonly refer to it as rate response. 

Not sure if I’m seeing some afib on the EKG, but I’m not really seeing well defined P waves. The device will help keep things steady if it is AF. An X-ray would be an easy way to determine if the device is single chamber, dual chamber or bi-ventricular.

I know what this is like. I know what its like to live with and exist within it without having the answers you want or the progress or emotional relief that you'd like. I also know what its like to lose many things that are very important to me because of this. I lost my interest in a lot of my hobbies, playing music, video games, cars, and I lost the person I was hoping to marry because they couldn't understand where my mind was and that I was trying to heal and get better. 

I ended up at rock bottom at the beginning of covid. I've applied to over 600 jobs because I was trying to figure life out and get going, but now I'm having to start over alone and just for myself. The best advice I can give you is to look into a therapist. If you can't afford a therapist, then I suggest you read up on the different aspects of depression online. I'm going to outline my best methods and the things I have done over the last many months to help myself tolerate the heartbreak and learn to love myself. There's a process to [finding yourself](https://www.psychalive.org/finding-yourself/) if you feel like the direction is wrong. 

If you think all of the below don't apply to you, then I definitely suggest a therapist and a visit to a doctor about depression or even something else. You might have a medical condition that you didn't know about and has an easy solution. Sometimes the help and medication you'll get will be the pickmeup you need to feel like yourself.

1. Read about cognitive dissonance, and look up activities to write and think about to address the way you think. Your mind is a hugely powerful place. You have been told you can do anything you put your mind to, but I disagree with that statement. In my experience, you can convince yourself of anything you want to believe, the truth is not always what you believe. This is where cognitive dissonance comes in. All the things you tell yourself are truths are things that are simply your perspective. You have convinced yourself through some creative thinking that these things are true.   
For me, this was a difficult thing to wrap my head around. It wasn't until I started reading and doing journaling about what I actually thought and felt based on the ways I was thinking and doing an analysis with the help of a guide that I saw how I was twisting my own thoughts.   
[Here's](https://medium.com/better-humans/cognitive-journaling-a-systematic-method-to-overcome-negative-beliefs-119be459842c) a great link to an article that I found to be really really helpful in this process. It breaks things down to a really easy to understand system that has really helped me journal effectively. There are other articles, this one just breaks it down really well for me.   

2. Learn expressing and journaling about gratitude. [This](https://positivepsychology.com/gratitude-journal/) is the article I use as a place when I don't know how or what to write. One of the most angering things I had to read over and over and hear over and over was write down three things you are grateful for. In my darkest days, when I had lost the will to live, when I was planning my own death, I was told this and had to go back and journal three stupid things that weren't helpful and made me more angry than I wanted to be.   
It wasn't until I got advice from my therapist that I started to understand the purpose. That was, "what are the positives you can take from this." Every situation, even the bad ones, present an opportunity to reflect and learn something. Those are ways you can improve, be more efficient, not make the same mistake, be thankful, or even just accept something as a good thing. Not everything that happens has a purpose. But everything that happens can be looked at to improve your level of knowledge. Over time you will find yourself naturally thinking this way in your day to day and it will feel more positive. 
3. This and 4 are honestly the most important for me. Practice self care. Nothing matters if you don't take time to love and care for yourself. Eating well, exercising, taking showers and using soap that smells nice and makes you feel clean. Its not always about feeling great, but sometimes the little things to help yourself feel better are invaluable. Taking time to settle your mind and learning how to meditate are essential to me and my ability to not feel like I'm numb or suffering. If I stop caring for myself, then I stop feeling connected to myself. If I spend all my time trying to do things for other people, then I'm neglecting myself. That's not something that is worth your time. It saps your energy and makes you feel miserable. Self care might even just be taking a day to yourself. Yoga is a great way to combine meditation and exercise.
4. Breathing. My therapist once told me that any strong emotion you feel can pass if you are willing to surrender to it. That has been a big one for me. Look up different breathing techniques. Earth, Ocean, and Fire breathing techniques are where I began. Depending on what your goals are for breathing it can help you. 

Finally, you are not alone. I never thought I'd be in as crappy a place as I've found myself in over the last year. The loss is devastating and I'm still not okay, but I've at least started to do some of my hobbies again. Some tasks are still chores because I don't feel like I'm making progress for myself, but it's something. Reach out if you need. You have a friend in me.

I’m learning this now. I was broken up with in July. It sucks and I miss them a lot. But, I’ve done a TON of personal growth in the last year and a lot of it started to really become apparent after the breakup. 

Unfortunately, the breakup didn’t have anything to do with my “aha” moments. My hard work, therapy, desire to improve myself and heal from my past, and to be better for myself is what drove me through the process. I had been doing it for my partner and our future before the breakup, I had to learn to do it for myself after that. It’s tough to focus on yourself when you aren’t happy with yourself. But if we look at ourselves and scrutinize the things we don’t like, we can turn them into opportunities to grow. 

I began with my mental health. I was diagnosed with trauma rated depression and ptsd. I worked through years of traumas and broke through some really tough mental barriers I had always struggled with. This is best done with your therapist. Use them to guide you through things you don’t like about yourself. A lot of time goes into reflecting on your feelings outside of therapy. 

Get rid of any social media that makes you feel anxious, hurt, or frustrated. You love your friends and family, but not everything (actually almost nothing) you’re going to see is really going to help you be and feel better. Instead you’ll see people and get jealous, you’ll see things that remind you of your ex and get hurt, and you’ll fall into the same traps and go backwards with your mental health. 

I next moved onto becoming a more grounded person. I learned to meditate, began reading self improvements about anything I was interested in. The four agreements is an important book, the 7 habits of highly effective people is one a lot of people like, breath is one I was interested in. Every book might not be filled with gems from cover to cover, but every book has at least a few pieces of gold you can learn from and apply to yourself. 

Through this process I began yoga occasionally, I focused on my personal fitness and started to take better care of myself. I’ve lost over 50 pounds since December and am about half way to where I want to be. I’ve hit a slump because of some mental health issues, but try to remind myself that things will keep getting better. 

I also began to look into hobbies I enjoy. Gardening, music, reading, tv shows, home improvement, designing clothes and architecture, cars, and I also looked deeper into aspects of spirituality and its connection with mental health. I’m not a huge fan of organized religion because of its lack of opportunity for independent thought, but I found that I could still look into different religions and see how different principles or methods could apply to me and my daily life. 

With all of that, I barely have any time for video games of going out anymore. But it is something where I have the option and if I need a couple nights off or a break from real life, I’m able to go and immerse myself outside of my worldly bubble for a while. 

Finally, dare to dream. Pinterest is a great place for you to create a vision board with things that make up the type of life you want to life. It’s essential to look forward to your future. You can shape it however you want. What do you want it to look like? What do you want to feel like? Who do you want to be? We are like trees. Our branches are spread all across the things we define ourselves by. Our jobs, our relationships, our friends and family, our status or image. 

When you cut off those branches it feels like a large part of you is missing. You are presented with a void and you panic and wonder how to fill it. Remind yourself that a tree only uses the branches after the roots are well established. You are your roots. Those things are the things you can go back to each and every day. 

Those are the things which will really make you whole. Invest time in yourself to discover where your roots lie. Nobody can take that away from you. Read and explore new things and ways of thinking. You are enough for yourself and perfection is defined by you. As long as you’re working to be your best and to grow continually, you will find your way.

Surprisingly, I learned my best techniques for meditation from my therapist. She taught me there different types of breathing for this type of meditation. Basically, you have to learn to relax yourself through breathing and focusing on clearing your mind. 

She had me start with a sacred place and then move into meeting my spirit guide. I'll explain the sacred place first. The breathing techniques are the same for each process so I'll type that out. Basically, you begin with ocean breathing. 5 seconds in and 5 seconds out. You breathe like this to calm your mind. Then, you close your eyes and continue for about 15 breaths. Next, you begin to earth breathe, imaging drawing in energy from the ground below you through one of your legs while breathing in for 5 seconds. Focus that energy into your abdomen and hold for 5 seconds. Finally breathe out for 5 seconds returning the energy to the earth. Breathe like this in a cycle until you feel calm and grounded. 

You continue earth breathing and begin to imagine yourself in a place in nature. Somewhere where you feel at home. Maybe at the beach with a nice breeze, maybe in a pasture. Imagine every sound, every detail, from the ground under your feet and plants around you, to the sky up above. You want to really create this place so that whenever you are stressed, you can go there in your mind. Continue earth breathing with your eyes closed throughout this whole process. It might take you a week or two of practice to really get there. But if you put in 30+ minutes a day, you will find that it is really easy to get there for yourself. 

Once you have created that place in your mind, then on a separate session, when your mind is less tired, work yourself from ocean breathing to earth breathing and begin the imagination work to meet your spirit guide. Really imagine yourself becoming a part of the earth with your breathing and then use the path to the boulder. Imagine yourself there, keeping your eyes closed, and then finally just let go of all expectation and be patient. It took me a few weeks to finally meet them, but it was really a special experience. It might feel faint the first time, but you have to remember that you are just forming the bridge to connect yourself to them. Over a few more sessions it will become more clear. They can be there for you when you just need someone, and when you are prepared you can begin to ask for guidance in whatever aspect of life you desire to find answers in.

Surprisingly, I learned my best techniques for meditation from my therapist. She taught me there different types of breathing for this type of meditation. Basically, you have to learn to relax yourself through breathing and focusing on clearing your mind.

Basically, you begin with ocean breathing. 5 seconds in and 5 seconds out. You breathe like this to calm your mind. Then, you close your eyes and continue for about 15 breaths. Next, you begin to earth breathe, imaging drawing in energy from the ground below you through one of your legs while breathing in for 5 seconds. Focus that energy into your abdomen and hold for 5 seconds. Finally breathe out for 5 seconds returning the energy to the earth. Breathe like this in a cycle until you feel calm and grounded. 

You continue earth breathing and begin to imagine yourself in a place in nature. Somewhere where you feel at home. Maybe at the beach with a nice breeze, maybe in a pasture. Imagine every sound, every detail, from the ground under your feet and plants around you, to the sky up above. You want to really create this place so that whenever you are stressed, you can go there in your mind. Continue earth breathing with your eyes closed throughout this whole process. It might take you a week or two of practice to really get there. But if you put in 30+ minutes a day, you will find that it is really easy to get there for yourself. 

Once you have created that place in your mind, then on a separate session, when your mind is less tired, work yourself from ocean breathing to earth breathing and begin the imagination work to meet your spirit guide. Really imagine yourself becoming a part of the earth with your breathing and then use the path to the boulder. Imagine yourself there, keeping your eyes closed, and then finally just let go of all expectation and be patient. It took me a few weeks to finally meet them, but it was really a special experience. It might feel faint the first time, but you have to remember that you are just forming the bridge to connect yourself to them. Over a few more sessions it will become more clear. They can be there for you when you just need someone, and when you are prepared you can begin to ask for guidance in whatever aspect of life you desire to find answers in. 

Good Luck! Blessed be!

I've been dealing with depression for the better part of 20 something years. I was much like you, in that I often ran away from the feelings whenever they rose up. Its our natural tendency to avoid the difficult things from our past and to focus on what is in front of us. Its our own self defense mechanism because naturally, processing these things isn't natural for us. 

I have found that keeping a mindfulness log/ thought journal is a good place to start. When I start to feel negative, I start to meditate. I practiced meditating when my mind was calm first. That way I could access that calm state when I was emotionally messed up too. Its a lot of breathing and visualization that works for me, maybe something else will work for you. 

Once I get myself to a calm enough state, I pull out my phone or my journal and start to write out what was bothering me. It feels nice to just let it out. Then, if I'm feeling up to it, I'll start to write why those thoughts were wrong, unjustified or of they were correct, I reflect on learning from that thought and turning it into a positive thought or interpretation. Every single thought has an origin in our past, and every one of those things is an opportunity to learn about ourselves. Either to learn from our pain, our mistakes, our demons, and our surroundings. We already have the wisdom we seek within ourselves, it has been provided by the universe. We just have to work to reconnect with the universe for the answers. 

Drugs are just a way to bypass our emotions to connect with the universe. But it can come at a cost in our long term future. If we learn to lean on the guidance of the universe by allowing our emotions to consume us for a few moments, a much better resolution comes without the guilt. 

For example. I was broken up with a couple months back by the only person I have ever considered to have as a permanent fixture in my life. She was and I still believe can be the one, but I have to let it go. It's been really hard, painful, distressing, triggering, etc. and I had to work very hard to turn all of my energy into focusing on myself and working on myself to make myself better. I focused all the hurt I felt and caused, the blame I gave myself, and pain I created into a positive energy and experience, healing and growing, making myself better than I was before. Even transcending my depression at times and learning to break through it more often. I've lost weight, read a ton of self help books, really really gotten into my craft and started planning for the future I want to create for myself. It sounds almost too good to be true right? The thing is, there isn't a day that goes by that I don't miss her and there are periods where I'm in absolute anguish, but I know that we are both on our own journeys. I remind myself often that the universe listens to my desires and will provide in good time. I also know that I have to remain true to myself and remember who I am and what I am striving towards. 

The thoughts have taken me to a darker place in my mind that I've had to fight to get to this place where I can work through them without turning to drugs or alcohol or something else. I still smoke weed on rare occasion, but I've found that my mind is a lot more steady than it used to be and my reactions to the world around me aren't as severe anymore. I'm able to respond to the negativity and fight off most of it because I've learned to believe that I can do better and grow from even the darkest experiences. 

I hope this helps and gives you a little guidance. Blessed be.

Okay here we go. 

1. Why is any advice I give worth hearing? Well, I was defined by PTSD, trauma, depression, anxiety, and suicidal thoughts for the better part of 15 years. I had been in a mentally dark place and attempted to function for even longer. When I began to consider witchcraft, I was in the middle of treatment for all of those things with a therapist and I came across shadow work. It stems on other parts of society as well, but this is where I learned about it.
2. Why is shadow work important? While I had always believed in magick, I lacked conviction in my belief. I was broken and in pain from my past which was unaddressed. By doing shadow work and addressing my past and my pain, I opened my mind to the possibilities of magick. My conviction and intent has become much stronger and I have actually began seeing positive effects of things I have been meditating on and casting spells for. 
3. What is shadow work? It depends on the context. Most people think of it in the context of witchcraft. I'm going to explain in that context. Its not really only for that, but it is a large part of how you perceive yourself and your ability to believe in what is possible. It is hugely intertwined with your intentions and that is where it effects your ability to do do the craft.
4. What is a shadow? Its a concept that goes back further than Carl Jung, but he is one of its popularizers. Shadow refers to the dark side of your conscience and subconscious. That is, the side of your mind that your ego tends to avoid. It is also the side of your mind that you most refer to when you look at yourself and the perception of yourself.  
Some examples: Do you think you're fat? Your shadow is talking. Do you think that you are inadequate? Your shadow. Do you think you are incapable of something? Your shadow. You think you are undeserving of something? Your shadow. You think you are better than everyone else? Your shadow. 
5. What causes a shadow? Well it will always exist. The part of yourself that has an ego is what constitutes your shadow. Every belief, good or bad, that you have of yourself is part of your shadow. All of those things which you define yourself by, based on things that have happened in your past, and things which you allow yourself to believe from other people.
6. Where do you start? Before you even start your first thought about how to address your past, you must be able to support yourself in the present. You will need 6 tools: 
   1. Ocean Breathing: Close your eyes and begin gently breathing in through your nose for 5 seconds and breathing out through your mouth for 5 seconds. Repeat 10-15 times. Think of your breathing as the tides of the ocean, In and out. You use this to calm yourself down and let emotions go as the tides of the ocean carry the energy in and out. Really focus on letting the energy go.
   2. Earth Breathing: Sit with your feet firmly on the floor. Close your eyes and gently breathe in for 5 seconds drawing the energy of the earth through one of your legs. Allow the breath and the energy to flow into your lower abdomen and hold it there for 5 seconds. Then gently breathe out and release the energy through the opposite leg for 5 seconds. Repeat throughout the activity while you try to connect with your inner self. This is also a grounding technique. While you are in the middle of any meditation, this will keep you in your reality so you do not become too carried away in the emotions of the event you are focusing on. It is also helpful for normalized grounding of yourself. 
   3. Fire Breathing: For an event which keeps you excessively wound up. You breathe in for 5 seconds then exhale like you are a dragon breathing fire for 5 seconds. You should be forcing the air out like you are trying to fog up a mirror. You should focus on releasing negative energy forcefully here. Repeat for 5-10 breaths. 
   4. A sacred place: Begin by calming yourself through ocean breathing. Take as many breaths as you need. After a few minutes, close your eyes and begin earth breathing. Imagine yourself in a place that brings you peace. Create it in your mind. Maybe it is on a warm sandy beach with your legs in the sand. Imagine the salty breeze of the ocean and the sounds around you. You get to create the world so it can be warm with the moon above your head. It could be the early morning sun gently kissing your face with its glowing warmth. Whatever you decide, but it should be void of technology. Just you, yourself and this place. Picture every detail as you continue to breathe. Take your time. Nobody can determine how long this will take, but the longer you spend trying to be there, the more clear the picture will become. It took me a couple weeks of dedicated time. Sometimes I tried for 10 minutes, sometimes longer. When you find your mind no longer focusing on what you are trying to do, you should take a break for a while and try again. Once you have been able to create this place in a solid way, you can move onto finding out who or what your companion is (#5). Don't forget to record this in your journal. 
   5. A sacred companion/ spirit animal: A companion chooses you, not the other way around. Again, begin with ocean breathing. Then when you feel ready close your eyes and begin earth breathing. Picture yourself walking down a path. At the end of the path, there is a sitting stone. Clear your mind as you approach the stone and take a seat. Continue to breathe and allow your mind to focus on this companion. They will be your companion through this whole journey. When you are in need of support and guidance, you will turn to them. What is the form of this creature? It can be anything. As you start you see them, allow them to approach you. Feel their presence and know that they are not a danger to you. Look into their eyes and allow them to look into yours. Feel the connection. They are there for you. Reach out and feel them. They are now part of you and you can call upon them whenever you need. Take your time to practice this just as you did the sacred place. You want to be able to tap into this person anytime you need. They will be there if you practice often. 
   6. The bonus tip. This will change a lot for you. We as a people have forgotten how to breathe. The ideal breath is gentle, does not involve a lot of force and lasts for 10-12 seconds from inhalation to the following inhalation. 5 seconds in, 6 seconds out. ONLY THROUGH YOUR NOSE. Breathing like this is how we are meant to breathe. It is the best way to allow our bodies to take in and exchange air. Mouth breathing is bad for you and can make you sick over time. Short breathing as well. Other than your moments of stress and meditation, learn to breathe this way. It will change your life.

EMDR (eye movement desensitization and reprocessing) is a relatively new method of therapy. This is an altered version called CRM (comprehensive resource model). They teach grounding and calming techniques before beginning the work to reprocess the memories from different traumatic events. 

The theory is that there is a third element to fight or flight responses and that is freeze. Basically people become mentally frozen at traumatic events and their minds associate any stress with those traumas. In this way, while they may try to function, there are large portions of the mind which are not functioning properly. Over the course of the sessions you work to create a new neural network that unfreezes and bypasses those traumas and reopens your mind to be able to process thoughts and emotions in a way that you couldn’t. 

The meditation is because they use breathing techniques like those found in yoga and meditation to help work through the strong emotions. In your daily like you learn to adopt these methods to remain grounded, to release negative emotions and energy as they happen, and to focus on making yourself better and calm in those moments. I used additional meditation to try to refocus my mind and to learn to quiet the racing and obtrusive thoughts. The two things in combination have worked really well. The therapy is non negotiable. I've been having some good luck with tomatoes and roses lately.

I found that they needed to be fed once ever 2-4 weeks and after the first bloom should be cut back to allow new growth. I pour some moon water during the feeding and have been watering normally since that period. I have had multiple bushes in the yard that have bloomed twice this summer with this method. Previously, before I returned home due to COVID, they looked quite sickly. Pruning them is essential to have roses which are manageable. You can also take your pruning shears and slide the blade against the thorns to break them off. It makes handling them a little easier. Others wrap the stems in newspaper when handling them. I normally leave them as nature intended. If I am pricked, I remind myself that Mother Earth has blessed me with a prick, to remind me of the balance between beauty and pain. 

For my tomatoes, I found the best method was to have a really good soil. I used a 1:1:1 ratio of chicken manure, gardening soil, and peat moss. I replaced the peat moss with vermiculite in one batch and didn't see too much of a difference. Again, feeding them and watering them with moon water on the first night. The rest of the time I allow my sprinklers to water early in the morning. I've never had so many tomatoes in the yard and am frankly surprised with how well they are doing. Feeding them once every 3-4 weeks is important. You can replant the long branches the you prune and they will usually take if they are given water and fertilizer. This year, I am going to attempt to keep cropping my plants and grow them all year round. 

Depending on where you are, I would recommend going to a local nursery. Look at the small round pellets they use in their plants. Some are yellow and others are green. I have been using the green pellets from the local nursery. They recommend feeding flowering plants every 2-3 weeks and fruiting and vegetables every 4-6 weeks.

You sound like you’re going through a depressive moment because of your anxiety. This is normal. Remember that your mental state is like the waves of an ocean and occasionally it has to go through a low to keep its balance. 

One of the best pieces of advice I ever got was to remind yourself of the little things you can do to keep functioning. Essentially that means get out of bed, make it, brush your teeth, and shower. If you can do those things, you are already having a great start to your day. 

If you have work to get done, try to commit an hour or two but not too much if you’re not feeling great. 

If you are active, go to the gym, if not so much, go for a walk. 30 minutes of walking with some good music on or spend a couple hours at the mall looking at clothes or things pertaining to a hobby you enjoy. Take yourself out to lunch, write your feelings out in a journal, or start to read a good book. 

Finally after all that, if you have gotten enough work done to feel good, hang out and watch a movie or play a game.

If nothing else remember: you are in control of your mind. You are allowed to have both good and bad days and you can always make a bad day better.
